findings.title: INCORRECT Tavily MCP tool ID conversion - canonical form uses hyphens, not underscores
findings.evidence: Diff proposes: `mcp__tavily__tavily_search` and `mcp__tavily__tavily_extract` (underscores). Official Tavily MCP docs (https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/mcp, https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-mcp) specify tool names as `tavily-search` and `tavily-extract` (hyphens). Repo canonical form in deep-research.md:6-7 and deep-research-agent.md:6-7 uses `mcp__tavily__tavily-search` (hyphen). QA report telemetry lines use underscores for logging/metrics only, not tool invocation.
findings.why: The diff changes all 8 RF agent files from the correct hyphenated form (`tavily-search`) to an incorrect underscored form (`tavily_search`). Official Tavily MCP documentation and existing codebase agents (deep-research.md, deep-research-agent.md) consistently use hyphens. The author's claim that hyphens "do not resolve" contradicts both upstream specification and working usage in this repo's deep-research agents. This will break Tavily MCP tool resolution at runtime.
findings.recommendation: REJECT this PR. The hyphenated form `mcp__tavily__tavily-search` / `mcp__tavily__tavily-extract` is correct per official Tavily MCP spec and is already working in deep-research.md and deep-research-agent.md. If the author encountered resolution issues, investigate the runtime environment or MCP server version, not the tool ID spec.

cross_cutting_observations.title: All 8 files consistently changed (scope claim verified), but in the WRONG direction
cross_cutting_observations.why: The author correctly changed all 8 files uniformly and made no other edits (scope discipline: excellent). However, the uniform change moves FROM the correct canonical form (hyphens, matching deep-research agents and official Tavily MCP spec) TO an incorrect form (underscores). Mechanical consistency does not fix semantic incorrectness. The diff shows 40+ line changes across frontmatter `tools:` lists, prose instructions, and Critical Rule clauses - all replacing hyphen with underscore. Zero non-Tavily changes detected (author's "ONLY" claim verified).
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: The PR demonstrates good mechanical discipline (uniform treatment, no scope creep) but catastrophic semantic error (wrong canonical form). REJECT and reverse: if any fix is needed, it should change the 8 RF agents FROM underscores (if present) TO hyphens to match deep-research.md. However, HEAD shows all 8 files already use hyphens correctly, so this PR inverts working state into broken state.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Frontmatter `tools:` list validity - incorrect IDs will fail agent spawn validation
cross_cutting_observations.why: Agent frontmatter `tools:` lists declare the MCP tools available to that agent. When SuperClaude or /task skill spawns an agent (e.g., `Agent: rf-qa`), the runtime validates requested tools against the session's available tool surface. If `mcp__tavily__tavily_search` (underscore) is listed but the MCP server exposes `mcp__tavily__tavily-search` (hyphen), the tool-not-found error will either prevent agent spawn or silently drop the tool, forcing fallback to WebSearch/WebFetch even when Tavily is available. This violates the Tavily-first protocol in all 8 agents' Critical Rules.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Confirm that agent `tools:` frontmatter entries exactly match the runtime tool IDs exposed by loaded MCP servers. Use `superclaude mcp --list` or session introspection to verify. The hyphen form is canonical per Tavily upstream; underscore form will fail validation unless a non-standard MCP bridge rewrites tool names (unlikely and undocumented in this repo).

notes_for_orchestrator: CRITICAL BLOCKER: This PR inverts the correct Tavily MCP tool IDs (hyphens) into an incorrect form (underscores), contradicting official Tavily MCP documentation (https://docs.tavily.com/documentation/mcp, https://github.com/tavily-ai/tavily-mcp) and the working canonical form already present in deep-research.md and deep-research-agent.md. The author's claim that hyphens 'do not resolve' is unsubstantiated and contradicts evidence. All 8 RF agent files are changed uniformly (good discipline) but in the WRONG direction (catastrophic semantic error). RECOMMENDATION: REJECT PR #197 AGENTS chunk. If resolution issues exist, debug the MCP server/runtime configuration, not the tool ID spec.
